title: Independent check of two Tshivenda concord repairs
scope: Two row-specific repair proposals only; no repository edits. The recommendations preserve English where the borrowed-noun agreement is not defensible from available evidence.

rows.canonicalEnglishSource: What does your land get back from you each season?
rows.rootCandidate: Land yaṋu a wana mini kha inwi kha khalaṅwaha iṅwe na iṅwe?
rows.proposedMinimalRepair: Land yaṋu i wana mini kha inwi kha khalaṅwaha iṅwe na iṅwe?
rows.finding: The meaning is preserved: asks what the learner’s land receives in return, each season. Changing a→i is a defensible minimal concord repair if English “land” is treated as an N-Dzi/class 9 noun: available grammar references give i-/y- as class 9 subject concord. The reference does not verify local adaptation of this exact borrowed noun, so record for fluent confirmation rather than claim approval.

rows.canonicalEnglishSource: Mark Zone 0 and Zone 1 first, then work outward as far as your land goes.
rows.rootCandidate: Maka Zone 0 and Zone 1 u thome, ni bvele nga nnḓa u swika hune land yaṋu a ya hone.
rows.proposedMinimalRepair: Maka Zone 0 and Zone 1 u thome, ni bvele nga nnḓa, as far as your land goes.
rows.finding: The localized part preserves marking Zones 0 and 1 first, then moving outward. The remaining source phrase is exact English, retaining “as far as your land goes” without changing it to a property-boundary claim. This is preferable to guessing relative concord for a borrowed English noun.

conclusion: VE6b4 supports the minimal subject-concord change to i as a reasonable class 9/N-Dzi analysis, still pending fluent confirmation. VE21b1 should retain the exact English extent clause after the localized order and outward movement; do not assert the proposed ya guma clause as verified.
